title: How to Choose a Video Style for Your Slide Deck (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: How to Choose a Video Style
slides.notes: The same deck can feel like a product launch, a quiet documentary or a punchy social clip. It all depends on how it moves.

slides.title: Look and feel changes presentation, not message
slides.notes: Your content stays yours. The look changes the framing, the motion, how text arrives on screen, where captions sit, and the overall texture.

slides.title: Match the direction to the deck
bullets: Calm and cinematic: brand stories, research
Bold and energetic: social clips, promos
slides.notes: These are directions, not presets. Clean and corporate suits training. Calm and cinematic suits brand stories. Bold and energetic competes for attention in a feed.

slides.title: Three questions narrow it down
bullets: How much text is on your slides?
slides.notes: Ask where people will watch, write one word for how they should feel, and check your text. Denser slides need a clean or calm direction.

slides.title: One deck, two directions
slides.notes: On your launch page, the headline gets slow, confident movement. Cut to three slides for social, and it becomes Scheduling. Sorted. Same brand, two videos.

slides.title: Decide the direction, then see it
bullets: Write speaker notes in your tone
slides.notes: On Pro, a.i. directs your video, shaping each scene to the tone you chose. Try Basic first, no subscription needed, at powerpoint2vid.com.
